battle.name: 反納比斯戰爭
battle.theater: 敘利亞南部大馬士革盆地
battle.brief: 前195年，塞琉古四世之弟安提奧庫斯四世自羅馬出奔，投奔大馬士革的納比斯王，聯軍合圍被塞琉古將領據守的城邑，掘進破城並縱掠之。卡面的斯巴達長矛屬於安提奧庫斯率領的希臘方陣與僱傭步兵那一層：它代表成排的希臘重步兵，而真正決定攻城成敗的，是納比斯的輕騎弓兵與工兵。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方是塞琉古王國與納巴泰王國，但真正的樞紐在第三方羅馬。前195年的敘利亞只是《阿帕米亞和約》之後的殘餘：王室只保有安提阿與幼發拉底河上游的一小片土地，附庸只剩數個希臘化城邦，塞琉古四世是羅馬在安提阿扶植的傀儡，一切任命都得看羅馬元老院的眼色。納巴泰王國則已從佩特拉的帳篷王國變成以大馬士革為都的商路國家，王室收入大半靠阿拉伯南部到地中海的香料與沒藥商路上的關稅，境內有希臘化城市、有希臘語商人、有一支以輕騎弓兵為主、外加僱傭重步兵的軍隊。開戰的導火線是塞琉古王宮內的人事：安提奧庫斯四世自幼被扣在羅馬當人質，長年在羅馬貴族中長大，他姊姊勞迪刻死後，羅馬把他派回安提阿；捲入宮廷鬥爭的他被指控圖謀不軌，轉而與納比斯結盟，回頭去攻擊塞琉古四世的人與城。帕提亞在東北方向觀望，沒有直接捲入；卡帕多細亞與亞美尼亞的關係也隨塞琉古勢力萎縮而鬆動。於是這一戰表面是兩國相爭，實質是羅馬的附庸秩序與納巴泰的商路帝國在敘利亞南方的正面碰撞。
countriesEn: The combatants in this war were the Seleucid kingdom and the Nabataean kingdom, but the real pivot lay with a third party, Rome. The Syria of 195 BC was only the remnant left after the Treaty of Apamea: the royal house kept a small tract around Antioch and the upper Euphrates, the client kingdoms were reduced to a handful of Hellenised cities, and Seleucus IV was a puppet installed at Antioch by Rome, whose appointments were made with one eye on the Roman Senate. The Nabataean kingdom, by contrast, had turned from a tent kingdom at Petra into a commercial state centred on Damascus: most of the royal revenue came from tolls on the incense and myrrh routes running from southern Arabia to the Mediterranean, and the kingdom contained Hellenised cities, Greek-speaking merchants, and an army whose backbone was light cavalry and archers supplemented by hired heavy infantry. The trigger lay in the personnel of the Seleucid court. Antiochus IV had been held in Rome as a hostage since childhood and grew up among the Roman elite; after the death of his sister Laodice the Romans sent him to Antioch. Dragged into the struggles of the court he was accused of plotting, and he allied himself with Nabis and turned back against the men and the city of Seleucus IV. Parthia watched from the north-east without entering the war, and the ties of Cappadocia and Armenia loosened as Seleucid power contracted. What looked like a clash between two states was in fact a collision between the Roman client order and the commercial empire of the Nabataeans over the southern approaches of Syria.
people: 主角是三個人。納比斯是當時最剽悍的阿拉伯系君主，以輕騎分隊劫掠、以另一部守土的用法令行省聞名，軍隊核心是帶短標槍與小盾的騎兵和用複合弓的弓兵；安提奧庫斯四世是塞琉古三世的幼子，自幼在羅馬當人質，靠希臘式修辭與羅馬貴族的交情取得影響力，回到敘利亞後卻迅速樹敵；塞琉古四世本人是安提阿宮廷裡最無力的一位君主，靠羅馬撐腰坐穩王位，最後死在自己宮廷的陰謀裡。包圍大馬士革的敘利亞方將領是腓尼基裔的將軍狄俄尼西俄斯，另有王室財務官赫拉克萊得斯等人；策動弒君的是宮相埃皮革涅斯。之後是大馬士革城中的守軍與工匠：守軍在城頭撐了數月，最後仍擋不住從地底來的破城法，城的財物在劫掠中被搬空，至於有多少工匠隨軍被帶往阿拉伯的佩特拉，史料並沒有交代。史料方面，這一戰的細節幾乎全靠波里比烏斯《史》第五、六卷；他既寫過安提奧庫斯四世在羅馬的朋友，也到過敘利亞，所以各方的說法在他筆下都帶著偏袒。
peopleEn: Three men dominate the story. Nabis was the most dashing of the Arab rulers of his day, celebrated for splitting his forces into raiding columns and a force that held the homeland, his army's core being cavalry with short javelins and small shields and archers using the composite bow. Antiochus IV, the youngest son of Antiochus III, had been a hostage in Rome since childhood and had learnt to work on Roman sentiment with Greek rhetoric, but back in Syria he made enemies faster than he made allies. Seleucus IV himself was the most dependent ruler in the house of Seleucus, propped up by Rome and finally killed in a conspiracy of his own court. On the Seleucid side the commander of the besieged city was the general Dionysius the Phoenician, with the royal treasurer Heracleides and others inside Damascus; the man who set the assassination in motion was the minister Epigenes. After them come the defenders of Damascus, its garrison and its craftsmen: the garrison held out for months on the walls and could not prevent the breach that came up from below the ground. The city was stripped in the sack, and as to how many craftsmen were carried off to Petra in Arabia, the sources do not say. As for the record itself, nearly every detail of this war comes from Polybius, who wrote about the friends Antiochus IV had in Rome and had himself seen Syria, so that every party's version reaches us through a man not neutral towards any of them.
kits: 卡面這件斯巴達長矛，在這場戰爭裡的位置需要說清楚：它不是納比斯的武備，而是這場戰爭的希臘化外殼。兩米長的槍身、銅套尾端，是古希臘重步兵方陣的標準兵器，動作是挺槍前推、以盾護身；前195年的塞琉古方陣早已改用更長的薩里沙長槍，但兩者同源，安提奧庫斯四世在羅馬時耳濡目染的正是這套希臘步兵傳統，與他後來在安提阿徵集的希臘與馬其頓僱傭兵所用的仍是同類長槍，配圓盾、科林斯式青銅頭盔與護脛。真正的主戰兵力是別的東西：納比斯一方的輕騎用短標槍與小圓盾，弓兵用複合弓，攻城時以工兵開掘坑道、破城而入，這些都不在方陣的射程之內。攻城器械與守具同樣值得記下：大馬士革有石造城牆與沿牆的塔樓，守方以投射武器與出擊拖住圍城者，圍城方則在城外築壘、斷絕出入城的大道、控制城郊水源與高地，並在夜裡發動襲擊。塞琉古王室的馬隊是另一個支點：安提阿的皇家馬廄養著來自高原的尼薩安馬，重騎與鎧甲騎兵是塞琉古軍的骨幹，納比斯的輕騎正是靠機動與地形避開這種正面衝撞。糧食與水是第三個環節：圍城方要從敘利亞南部運糧，而攻城季節正逢地中海東岸的乾熱，商路與水源的爭奪同樣決定勝負。
kitsEn: The place of the Spartan dory in this war has to be stated carefully: it was not Nabis' weapon but the Hellenic casing of the war itself. The two-metre shaft with its bronze butt-cap was the standard arm of the Greek hoplite phalanx, used to push the spear forward behind the shield; by 195 BC the Seleucid phalanx already carried the longer sarissa, but the two belonged to the same tradition, and the hoplite array Antiochus IV had grown up with in Rome was the same array his Greek and Macedonian mercenaries carried into Syria at Antioch, with the same class of long spear, the round aspis, the Corinthian bronze helmet and greaves. The real weight of battle lay elsewhere. Nabis' light horse went into action with short javelins and small round shields, his archers used the composite bow, and the siege was won by engineers driving a gallery under the walls, none of which was within the reach of a phalanx. The siege equipment and the defences are worth recording in their own right. Damascus had a stone curtain and towers along the wall; the defenders used missile troops and sallies to hold the besiegers off, and the besiegers in turn threw up lines in the outer ring, cut the great roads out of the city, held the water and the heights around it, and launched attacks by night. The royal cavalry of the Seleucids was another pivot: the stud at Antioch kept horses from the Iranian plateau, and the heavy and armoured horse formed the backbone of the Seleucid army, exactly the sort of charge that Nabis' light horse dodged by mobility and by ground. Supply and water formed the third ring: the besiegers had to bring grain up through the southern part of Syria, and the season of the siege fell in the dry heat of the eastern Mediterranean, so the contest for roads and for water decided as much as the fighting did.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術核心是合圍與掘進。納比斯與安提奧庫斯的聯軍抵達大馬士革後，沒有立刻強攻，而是先在外圍分段築壘、封鎖出入城的大道，並派輕騎巡邏切斷城市與腹地的聯絡；安提奧庫斯帶來的是希臘式的攻城習慣，攻城方真正的技術手段是掘進：在城牆外側找到巖層，挖出通往牆基的坑道，填平壕溝之後從內部破壞牆基，再以全軍衝入缺口。城破之後是劫掠與整編，而不是長期的圍城消耗。守方的戰術是以城牆與城頭的投射武器拖住時間，配合出城反擊；大馬士革守軍沒有得到決定性的援軍，狄俄尼西俄斯被圍在城內，外援的路線被封住。到了安提奧庫斯奪取王位之後，戰爭性質變成第二階段：他轉而懷疑起曾幫助自己的納比斯，集結兵馬準備對付阿拉伯方向，而就在這個節骨眼上，他在大馬士革被自己城中的居民所殺，納比斯得以脫身，戰事就這樣在沒有會戰的狀態下收場。羅馬在整場衝突中沒有出兵，只以使節與書信影響敘利亞政局，這是本戰最特別的一點：戰爭的勝負其實由安提阿的宮廷政變決定。
tacticsEn: The tactical core of this war was encirclement and mining. When the allied forces of Nabis and Antiochus reached Damascus they did not strike at once, but raised lines in the outer ring, sealed the great roads out of the city section by section, and sent light cavalry to cut the city's contact with the hinterland. Antiochus brought with him the Greek habit of siege, and the technical instrument of the besiegers was the mine: a gallery was driven through the rock outside the wall, the ditch was filled, the base of the curtain was hollowed out from within, and the whole army went in through the breach. What came after the fall was sack and reorganisation rather than a long siege of attrition. On the defensive side the method was to hold the enemy off with missile troops from the wall and with counter-attacks, and to wait for relief; Damascus was given no decisive aid, Dionysius the Phoenician was shut up inside the walls, and the approaches of every relieving force were covered. When Antiochus took the throne the war changed character in its second phase. He began to suspect the very Nabis who had helped him, mustered troops against the Arab direction, and at that very moment he was killed in Damascus by the citizens of his own city. Nabis escaped intact, and the campaign closed without a set-piece battle. Rome fought none of it, influencing the politics of Syria only through envoys and letters, and that is the most peculiar feature of the whole affair: the outcome was decided by a palace conspiracy rather than by a battle.
data: 可以核對的數字有限，這場戰爭的史料主要出自一個人之手。時間：安提奧庫斯出奔納比斯並合圍大馬士革在前195年；塞琉古四世於前194年在安提阿被宮中陰謀者殺死；安提奧庫斯即位後在前193年被大馬士革的居民殺死於城內神廟。整場衝突自前195年至前193年，約兩年多。兵力：波里比烏斯沒有留下雙方兵力的確切數目，只說納比斯的軍隊規模不小、攻城時有工兵配合，並記載大馬士革被圍數月，因此不宜引用任何精確的人數。距離與地理：大馬士革位於安BAR條河的灌溉平原上，西面的安提阿與北面的阿勒頗各有數百公里之遙，東面通向幼發拉底河與美索不達米亞，東南是通往佩特拉的商道；這些距離決定了援軍能否趕到，也決定了圍城方必須靠封路而不是靠攻城速度取勝。物資：城破後的劫掠是這場戰爭在物質上唯一的大額變動，除此之外沒有可核的糧秣、錢幣或兵力數字。往後的坐標在前64年，龐培把納巴泰王國併入羅馬敘利亞行省，敘利亞南方的行政與駐軍才第一次有明確的編制。
dataEn: Few figures can be checked, because the evidence for this war comes down largely to a single man. Chronology: Antiochus fled to Nabis and the siege of Damascus began in 195 BC; Seleucus IV was killed in his own palace at Antioch in 194 BC; Antiochus was killed by the people of Damascus in a temple of the city in 193 BC. The whole conflict therefore runs from 195 to 193 BC, a little over two years. Numbers: Polybius gives no exact figure for the strength of either side, noting only that Nabis' army was not small, that engineers worked with it during the siege, and that Damascus was under siege for a period of months; it is better therefore to quote no precise headcount at all. Distance and geography: Damascus stands on the irrigated plain of the Barada, with Antioch several hundred kilometres to the west, Aleppo to the north, the Euphrates and Mesopotamia beyond it to the east, and the caravan road to Petra to the south-east. Those distances decided whether relief could arrive, and they forced the besiegers to win by cutting roads rather than by speed. Stores: the sack was the only large material change in the war, and beyond it there is no verifiable figure for grain, money or numbers of men. The later fixed point comes in 64 BC, when Pompey absorbed the Nabataean kingdom into the Roman province of Syria, and the administration and garrison of the southern Levant were for the first time set out in a regular order.
cause: 起因是多層的。第一層是《阿帕米亞和約》之後塞琉古王國的崩解：前190年塞琉古三世戰死，小亞細亞歸羅馬與佩加蒙，的美索不達米亞歸帕提亞，只剩一個以安提阿為核心的殘局；前194年塞琉古四世在羅馬的安排下即位，凡是對羅馬不忠的外交都會被視為背叛。第二層是安提奧庫斯四世的位置：他是最有希臘修養的塞琉古王子，也是羅馬人最熟悉的東方人質，在安提阿既無根基又有大量敵人；其姊勞迪刻死後，羅馬把他派去接替姊姊在王宮中的位置，宮廷立刻視之為權力入侵。第三層是納比斯的算盤：控制大馬士革就等於控制阿拉伯商路的北端出口，納巴泰人正需要一座可以徵稅、可以駐軍的大城來對付塞琉古與托勒密。第四層是宮廷陰謀本身：安提奧庫斯被指為圖謀不軌，羅馬又要求把他押回意大利處置；他寧可投奔阿拉伯人，也不肯被押走，於是所有矛盾在安提阿與大馬士革之間同時爆開。帕提亞與羅馬在遠方各自觀望，這一戰因此沒有第三方直接下場。
causeEn: The causes lie on several levels. The first is the collapse of the Seleucid state after the Treaty of Apamea: Antiochus III died in 190 BC, Asia Minor went to Rome and Pergamon, the Euphrates and Mesopotamia to Parthia, and nothing was left but a remnant centred on Antioch. Seleucus IV, a son of Antiochus III, was seated in 194 BC under Roman arrangement, and any diplomacy that seemed unfaithful to Rome was treated as betrayal. The second is the position of Antiochus IV. He was the most Hellenised of the Seleucid princes and also the easterner the Romans knew best, and in Antioch he had neither a base nor a shortage of enemies. After the death of his sister Laodice the Romans sent him to take his sister's place in the palace, and the court at once read the move as an intrusion of power. The third is Nabis' own calculation: control of Damascus was control of the northern outlet of the Arabian trade, and the Nabataeans needed a great city they could tax and garrison against the Seleucids and the Ptolemies. The fourth is the conspiracy itself. Antiochus was charged with plotting against the king, and Rome demanded that he be taken back to Italy for punishment; he preferred to throw in his lot with the Arab rather than be led away, so that every grievance in Antioch and Damascus came to a head at once. Parthia and Rome each watched from a distance and neither entered, and this is why no third state appears on the field.
impact: 直接影響是塞琉古王國的君主在幾年之內被換掉：前194年的塞琉古四世死於宮中陰謀，前193年的安提奧庫斯四世死於大馬士革的街頭，塞琉古王朝自此只剩一個孱弱的傀儡政權，直到前64年龐培把敘利亞變成羅馬行省，羅馬才不必再依賴某一位安提阿的君主。第二層影響落在納巴泰一方：大馬士革的城防被打殘、財富被洗劫一次，但納比斯保住了對敘利亞南方的控制與阿拉伯商路的北端，國力反而因為掌握了一段時期的貿易通道而上升；納巴泰人從此在敘利亞南部長期擔任羅馬與帕提亞之間的緩衝角色。第三層是希臘世界的技術與僱傭兵：圍城用的掘進技術、攻城方善於用工兵的作風，以及重步兵配合輕騎與投射兵的戰術組合，都在安提阿與大馬士革之間被反覆示範；安提奧庫斯四世之死後，敘利亞的宮廷與城邦再沒有一支能獨立抵抗的大型軍隊，僱傭兵將成為下一個世紀敘利亞戰爭的主要兵源。
impactEn: The immediate effect was that the ruler of the Seleucid house changed hands within a few years: Seleucus IV was killed by a palace conspiracy in 194 BC, Antiochus IV was killed in the streets of Damascus in 193 BC, and from then on the Seleucid monarchy was a weak client apparatus, until in 64 BC Pompey turned Syria into a Roman province and Rome no longer needed any particular ruler in Antioch. The second effect fell on the Nabataeans. The defences of Damascus were battered and its wealth stripped once, but Nabis kept his hold on southern Syria and on the northern end of the Arabian trade, and the state grew stronger on the strength of the transit it controlled for a time; the Nabataeans henceforth served for centuries as the buffer between Rome and Parthia in the south. The third effect belongs to the Greek world of technique and mercenaries. Mining under a wall, the practice of bringing engineers with the army, and the tactical combination of heavy foot with light horse and missile troops were all demonstrated again and again between Antioch and Damascus. After the death of Antiochus IV neither the court nor the cities of Syria possessed a field army capable of standing on its own, and hired troops would be the main military resource of the Syrian wars of the following century.
result: 結果沒有典型的勝負可言，因為這場戰爭的決定性時刻是在宮廷裡而不是在城牆下。大馬士革一度被圍、被掘進破城，並遭到劫掠；安提奧庫斯四世因此一度以塞琉古王族的身份出現在敘利亞南部，卻沒有得到王位。真正的轉折是前194年塞琉古四世在安提阿被殺，宮相埃皮革涅斯與將領狄俄尼西俄斯的陰謀成功；安提奧庫斯隨即在安提阿即位，隨後卻在準備對付納比斯的前夜，被大馬士革的居民殺死在城內神廟，據其後的記述，其屍身被撕碎焚燒。於是戰爭以一種對雙方都沒有決定性勝果的方式收場：納比斯保住大馬士革與商路，未被塞琉古吞併；塞琉古王朝換了主，但換上來的是更弱、更受羅馬約束的君主；希臘化的敘利亞從此進入長達半個世紀的慢性崩解，納巴泰王國也一路好到前64年龐培揮軍東來的那一年。
resultEn: The outcome cannot be described as a clear victory, because the decisive moment of this war happened inside a palace rather than in front of a wall. Damascus was besieged, entered by mine and sacked; Antiochus IV appeared for a time in southern Syria in the person of a Seleucid prince, but did not obtain the throne. The real turning point came in 194 BC, when Seleucus IV was killed at Antioch and the conspiracy of the minister Epigenes and the general Dionysius the Phoenician succeeded. Antiochus was then crowned at Antioch, and only shortly afterwards, as he was preparing to move against Nabis, he was killed by the inhabitants of Damascus in a temple of the city, his body being torn apart and burnt according to the later account. The war thus closed without a decisive result for either side. Nabis kept Damascus and the trade road and was not absorbed by the Seleucids; the Seleucid house changed its master, but the new master was weaker and more tightly bound to Rome; Hellenised Syria entered a long half-century of slow disintegration, and the Nabataean kingdom did well until the year in which Pompey came east.
